title: Units and conversions
summary: The conversions you need when manuals, labels and parts use different units: length, weight, volume, pressure, temperature, power, energy and the electrical basics.

steps.text: Find the row for what you have and multiply by the factor to get the other unit; divide to go back.
Round the answer to what you can actually measure.

notes:
## Multiply to convert

| From | To | Multiply by |
|---|---|---|
| Inches | Millimetres | 25.4 |
| Feet | Metres | 0.3048 |
| Miles | Kilometres | 1.609 |
| Pounds | Kilograms | 0.4536 |
| Ounces (weight) | Grams | 28.35 |
| US gallons | Litres | 3.785 |
| Imperial gallons | Litres | 4.546 |
| US fluid ounces | Millilitres | 29.57 |
| psi | bar | 0.0689 (1 bar is 14.5 psi or 100 kPa) |
| Horsepower | Watts | 746 |
| BTU per hour | Watts | 0.293 (1 W is 3.41 BTU/h) |
| Kilowatt-hours | Megajoules | 3.6 |
| Kilocalories | Kilojoules | 4.184 |
| Pound-feet (torque) | Newton-metres | 1.356 |

## Temperature

°C = (°F − 32) × 5 ÷ 9, and °F = °C × 9 ÷ 5 + 32. Landmarks: water freezes at 0 °C (32 °F) and boils at 100 °C (212 °F) at sea level; body temperature is 37 °C (98.6 °F); −40 is the same on both scales.

## Electrical basics

- Watts = volts × amps. Amps = watts ÷ volts.
- Volts = amps × ohms (Ohm's law).
- Watt-hours = volts × amp-hours. 2,000 mAh is 2 Ah; at 3.7 V that is about 7.4 Wh.
- The same power at 12 V takes 10 times the current it takes at 120 V, which is why low-voltage wiring has to be so much thicker.

## Energy in fuels (approximate)

| Fuel | Energy |
|---|---|
| Gasoline | About 34 MJ per litre (9.5 kWh) |
| Diesel | About 38 MJ per litre (10.7 kWh) |
| Propane | About 46 MJ per kg (about 25 MJ per litre of liquid) |
| Dry firewood | About 15–19 MJ per kg |

A small generator turns only about a fifth to a quarter of its fuel's energy into electricity.
